title: The enforced CSP still allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts, so it does not stop an injected inline script if any sanitizer ever slips.

source.ref: Whole-site audit 2026-11-16 (project thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: CONFIRMED. Audit file: audit/FINAL-BUILD-AND-REPAIR-LIST-2026-11-16.md

detail:
EVIDENCE: next.config.ts:36 script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' ... (comment at :31 says it is kept for Next's inline RSC scripts); the team already notes a nonce route at :139. I reviewed all ~60 dangerouslySetInnerHTML sinks: QR/SVG are server-generated, member rich text goes through sanitizeInlineHtml (lib/entity-blocks/block-content.ts:1031), library SVG through safeElementSvg/svg-sanitize, JSON-LD escapes '<' (components/json-ld.tsx:5). No exploitable sink found.

WHY IT MATTERS: Defence in depth only. Nonce-based CSP is a large change with checkout/Stripe interplay, so do it after launch.

FIX DIRECTION: Plan nonce-based script-src via proxy.ts after Jan 1; no action needed for launch.

2026-11-16 owner answer (Daniel, 15:01Z): move to nonce-based scripts, with a test run first and a rollback if anything breaks. This supersedes "after Jan 1" above.

2026-11-16 step 0 shipped, row stays OPEN (ADR-1954, docs/security/csp-nonce.md): the nonce-based policy is built (lib/security/csp-nonce.ts, called from proxy.ts) and is OFF. Two-step rollout, both switches blank by default and read through envFlag: (1) CSP_NONCE_REPORT_ONLY=1 sends the strict policy (nonce + 'strict-dynamic', no 'unsafe-inline' in script-src) as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only on member-app pages, beside today's enforced policy; reports reach /api/csp-report tagged policy=nonce. (2) CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE=1 enforces it on those pages, after the gate in docs/RUNBOOKS.md "Nonce-based script policy" (7 clean days, a preview check, the owner's go). Blank the switch and redeploy to roll back.

SCOPE, stated plainly: only pages under app/(main) get the nonce. Next 16 stamps a nonce only on per-request renders, and experimental SRI does not cover the inline RSC payload, so static and ISR pages (marketing, discover, help, share pages, Space websites) keep 'unsafe-inline'; removing it there would make them dynamic. This row closes when CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE is on in production. The verify probe reads the literal in next.config.ts, which stays for the static pages, so closing needs the owner's word on retiming that probe to the member-app policy.

NOT YET VERIFIED (the test run answers these): the analytics head script's hash across the proxy and page bundles; not-found pages under a member path; a real browser run with the policy on.

2026-11-18 step 1 STARTED (Daniel chose "Yes, start the test run" in the security and SEO/GEO thread, 17:59Z): CSP_NONCE_REPORT_ONLY=1 set on Vercel Production and Preview. Verified live at 18:11Z: production /events (deployment dpl_2kjsC2SkaYkaec8fqFUmz56Zv23S) sends Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only with a per-request nonce, 'strict-dynamic', 'report-sample' and the five root-script hashes, beside the unchanged enforced policy. Nothing is blocked. The seven-day gate in docs/RUNBOOKS.md "Nonce-based script policy" (section written by SEC-025) runs to 2026-11-25 at the earliest; watch runtime logs for csp.violation with policy=nonce. Row stays open until CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE is on.

2026-11-23 THE TEST RUN MEASURED NOTHING, AND THE 11-25 DATE IS OFF. 1,122 policy=nonce reports in 23 hours, all naming Next's own scripts. Read with test/e2e/csp-nonce.spec.ts (e2e manual, capture_shell on): production /feed in report-only mode had 1 of 117 scripts carrying the response's nonce. Cause: Next looks for the nonce in Content-Security-Policy first and in the report-only header only when that is absent, and on Vercel the render is handed the RESPONSE side's value under that name, which in the test run is next.config.ts's static policy (no nonce). So Next stamps nothing and every one of its scripts is reported. With the policy ENFORCED on a private preview (same spec) /feed had 110 of 117 nonced, 3 hashed, 2 data blocks, and one script left out: the analytics head script, whose hash never matched because it embedded three functions by toString() and the proxy and page bundles print them differently. That hash is fixed in the same PR as the spec (the three rules are string literals now, held to the real functions by cookie-consent.test.ts). The smoke suite failed the same 16 tests on that preview in both modes, so enforcing broke no page it loads. STILL OPEN: the seven clean days cannot be counted until the test run can see the nonce, which needs the enforced header on member pages to name it during the run. proxy-csp.test.ts pins the opposite ("the proxy must not replace the enforced policy during the test run"), so that change waits for the owner's word; the built patch is at /mnt/project-files/security/scan-1243-test-run-enforced-header.patch. Do not set CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE before the spec reads zero scripts left out on a preview with it on.

2026-11-23 14:00Z owner answer (Daniel, card: "Yes, fix the test run"): the test run may change the enforced header on member pages. Built: during the run the proxy sends buildCompatPolicy (lib/security/csp-nonce.ts) as Content-Security-Policy on member documents. script-src carries the nonce and the hashes so Next finds it; script-src-elem and script-src-attr restate today's rules, so a current browser allows what it allowed before. The one test that pinned the opposite (proxy-csp.test.ts, "the proxy must not replace the enforced policy during the test run") is rewritten on that answer, that case only. The seven days restart from the first production reading of bare=0 after this deploys.

2026-11-23 15:06Z FIRST PRODUCTION READING AFTER THE FIX, AND THE SEVEN DAYS START HERE. #5444 deployed (dpl_7fwEEcsGbSjAgGtNypW7aLvbaNkv). e2e (manual) run 45200760758 against frequencylocal.com, member session, report-only mode: /feed 119 scripts, 113 nonced, 4 hashed, 2 data blocks, 0 left out; /lead 112 / 106 / 4 / 2, 0 left out; /spaces/danieltyack 139 / 131 / 4 / 4, 0 left out. The smoke suite failed 20 tests on that run against 24 on the same morning's production run before any of this, the same tests, so nothing regressed. Runtime logs after the deploy carry no report naming a Next script. The policy=nonce reports that remain are also reported by the ENFORCED policy on the same request, so they are today's behaviour and not nonce gaps: eval in a shared chunk on a Space manage page, and connect-src to fonts.googleapis.com on /nearby (the Google map's own fonts). EARLIEST STEP 2: 2026-11-30, after seven days with no unexplained policy=nonce report, one preview with CSP_NONCE_ENFORCE=1 read with test/e2e/csp-nonce.spec.ts at 0 left out, and the owner's go.

verify.note: Fails on 2026-11-16 (audit run). Passes when the fix lands. Audit-written probes are direction checks; retime only with Daniel's phrase.
